transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Meeting recorded by Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orbis CTO), Tom Alvarez (Head of Infra), Liam Park (Product)

Summary: quick discovery on Private VPC deployment. Orbis wants private-only endpoints, strict data residency, and to understand network topology options. They mentioned benchmarking needs and some existing infra constraints.

00:00 Amy Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Amy from Redwood, i have Marcus with me, we are the AE/SE pair for this opp, thanks for taking time
00:08 Priya Nair: thanks Amy, we appreciate it. quick intro: i'm Priya, CTO at Orbis, we've got Tom for infra and Liam for product. we're exploring a private deployment for inference, mostly for PCI and some regulated PII workflows.
00:20 Amy Chen: great, super helpful. big picture - are you leaning hosted/dedicated/private, or still evaluating?
00:25 Priya Nair: leaning private. we want the control, also need EU data residency and a potential APAC location later. cost matters but security is the gating factor.
00:34 Marcus Li: quick q on traffic flow - do you want Redwood to sit inside your VPC (private endpoints, peered) or do you prefer a private egress path where we handle instances in our VPC with peering? basically peered vs transit gateway style.
00:50 Tom Alvarez: good question. our infra team prefers minimal cross-account exposure. we typically use VPC peering for low-latency internal traffic, but for many spokes we use Transit Gateway. curious about how Redwood handles scaling and cross-region models.
01:05 Marcus Li: ok. we support both patterns. for small number of VPCs peering is straightforward, if you have many accounts or want central routing then Transit Gateway works better. one note: cross-region peering has limits - we often recommend deploying Redwood nodes in the same region as the VPC to avoid cross-region egress.
01:20 Priya Nair: so are you able to deploy in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1? we need EU first.
01:28 Amy Chen: yes EU is supported for Private - we have regionized control plane options; APAC we can enable but it's typically on a lead time depending on capacity reservations. we'll surface exact region availability in the follow-up.
01:40 Liam Park: can you briefly explain the private endpoint setup? we use AWS but a lot of our services are inside private subnets, no internet access.
01:48 Marcus Li: sure - two common approaches: 1) AWS PrivateLink / Interface endpoints: we create ENIs in your VPC, traffic stays private. 2) VPC peering or Transit Gateway: Redwood services run in a customer-peered network. PrivateLink is nice for private-only connectivity without routing changes, but you need to manage ENIs and AZ coverage.
02:04 Tom Alvarez: any NAT concerns? our current pattern is S3 via gateway endpoints, and we lock egress with NAT in a few bastion subnets.
02:12 Marcus Li: yep we recommend keeping S3 via Gateway endpoints; for model downloads or image pulls we can use VPC endpoints or an internal blob store. if you want Redwood to never touch the public internet we can arrange for model artifacts to be pulled from your S3 via role-assumed access in-region.
02:30 Priya Nair: what about KMS? keys must be customer-managed, HSM-backed if possible.
02:36 Amy Chen: we integrate with customer KMS - customer-managed keys are supported for at-rest model encryption and artifact storage. HSM integrations are on the enterprise track; we'll confirm HSM partners in the security doc.
02:48 Marcus Li: small note - some customers use envelope encryption: your KMS protects the master key, Redwood manages data encryption keys in the private deployment but the master key never leaves your control.
03:00 Priya Nair: latency - our latency SLO for inference is <150ms p95 for EU users. how do you ensure model placement and caching?
03:10 Marcus Li: we do placement rules: pin a model regionally so the serving runtime lives in EU. we also do KV cache and prefix caching; for p95 latency you want local model placement + small batching windows. there's always a tradeoff with cost. we'll share suggested instance sizes and batching configs in the benchmarks.
03:28 Tom Alvarez: curious about throughput and autoscaling - when traffic spikes, does the peering create bursts of connections we need to allow?
03:36 Marcus Li: autoscaling will spin up workers in the same region. you'll need to ensure subnets/ENI limits and route tables are sized appropriately; if using PrivateLink add ENI quotas per AZ. we typically provide guidance for AWS limits in the runbook.
03:52 Liam Park: security controls - SSO, RBAC, audit logs - are those available in Private?
03:58 Amy Chen: yes SAML SSO, RBAC at token and team level, and detailed audit logs. for Private we ship logs to your logging destination via secure forwarders, or you can opt to store logs in our control plane depending on compliance requirements.
04:14 Priya Nair: does Redwood support sending logs to our Splunk cluster via a private endpoint?
04:19 Marcus Li: yes we can push over private connectivity. typically customers either use Kinesis/Firehose with VPC endpoints or a direct syslog forwarder inside their network. we'll include examples.
04:31 Tom Alvarez: about billing and metering, we need usage breakdown per team and per model - is that supported on Private?
04:38 Amy Chen: yes, per-token and per-route billing is available and we can push usage metrics to your monitoring via secure endpoints; also per-model dashboards in the Console if you run the private control plane.
04:50 Priya Nair: one compliance question: do you provide SOC2 reports and penetration test summaries?
04:55 Amy Chen: we do. i'll attach SOC2 type II, our pen test summary, and also the private deployment security pack in the follow-up.
05:03 Liam Park: performance testing: can we run benchmarks with our sample prompts? we want to compare latency against our current self-hosted runtime and Anthropic endpoints for some hallucination checks too.
05:12 Marcus Li: absolutely - common approach: we run a short pilot, deploy a model in your VPC, run synthetic and workload-based tests, and produce P95/P99 and throughput numbers. we'll need a test dataset and a small set of representative prompts.
05:26 Priya Nair: how long does a pilot usually take? can we do a two-week pilot?
05:30 Amy Chen: two weeks is doable for an initial perf pilot. full POC with security approvals can take longer depending on procurement.
05:38 Tom Alvarez: networking nuance - do you require static IPs on our side for peering or for firewall allow-lists?
05:44 Marcus Li: for PrivateLink you mainly open SGs and ENIs; for peering you control the routing. if you have restrictive firewalls we can provide the destination IP ranges; some customers use egress proxies and NAT to centralize outbound.
05:58 Priya Nair: data residency - we need guarantee that EU data stays in EU. do you support pinning control plane and data plane to regions?
06:05 Amy Chen: yes you can pin both. we have options: control plane in our EU region or a customer-managed control plane in your account. we'll detail tradeoffs in the doc.
06:18 Liam Park: are there gotchas around cross-account IAM roles for model artifact access?
06:22 Marcus Li: you'll need an IAM role allowing Redwood worker nodes to access artifacts in your account; we recommend a scoped role with least-privilege and short-lived creds. we'll share the CloudFormation snippet.
06:36 Tom Alvarez: curious about multi-region replication for model artifacts - we usually replicate S3 objects to eu-west and ap-southeast. any preference?
06:42 Marcus Li: replicate close to where you serve; that reduces startup latency when a worker pulls a cold model. we can also cache layers on local disks.
06:52 Priya Nair: any mention of open-source model support - we run a few Llama variants internally. will Redwood support quantized variants?
06:58 Marcus Li: yes, we support multiple model families and quantized variants. some optimizations vary by model; we'll share compatibility matrix.
07:08 Amy Chen: ok quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack, Marcus will prepare benchmark plan and instance recommendations, and Orbis to share VPC CIDR and region list. schedule a Marcus/Tom deep-dive next week.
07:24 Priya Nair: sounds good. thanks everyone.
07:28 Amy Chen: thanks - we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Notes: transcript contains typical speech artifacts and minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K V cache' or 'private link' spelled differently). References to shared artifacts: "security pack (link)" and "benchmark spreadsheet (link)" will be shared in follow-up email.

End of recording.
